question: Grandad smoked all his life and reached 90. In the 50-year study of British doctors, how much life did lifelong smokers lose?
answer: About 10 years. Lifelong smokers among the doctors died about a decade earlier than those who never smoked; stopping at 30 won back nearly all of it. On the study's survival chart about 1 smoker in 25 reached 90, against about 1 in 4 who never smoked. Grandad was the 1 in 25.
move: The one exception you remember hides the many you never met.
ask: Which risky habit do I excuse because I know one person it never seemed to hurt?
trap: About 2 years, since Grandad smoked and still reached 90.

notes: Four relatives each: one smoker reached 90, no non-smoker did. 25% against 0%.
40 each: 28% against 13%. The family story is already turning.
4,000 each: 24% against 4%, the doctors' figures. Grandad was the 1 in 25.

reference: Doll, Peto, Boreham & Sutherland, Mortality in relation to smoking: 50 years' observations on male British doctors, BMJ, 2004
